entities.summary:
Giovannino de' Grassi (fl. 1350s) was an Italian architect, sculptor, painter, and illuminator who made significant contributions to the development of Renaissance art in Southern Europe.

Born in the 14th century, de' Grassi's work had a lasting impact on the artistic landscape of Italy, particularly in the cities of Florence and Rome.

His innovative use of light and shadow in his paintings, as well as his skillful use of perspective, influenced a generation of artists, including Brunelleschi and Donatello.

Despite his significant contributions, de' Grassi remains somewhat of a forgotten figure in the annals of art history, with many of his works destroyed or lost over the centuries.
